label: Git
headline: Git Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for the Git commands you reach for every day — from initializing repos to branch management, history inspection, and collaboration.

items.name: git init
items.definition: Initialize a new local repository in the current (or named) directory.

items.name: git clone
items.definition: Download a full copy of a remote repository to your machine.

items.name: git clone (named)
items.definition: Clone a remote repository into a custom-named local directory.

items.name: git status
items.definition: Show which files are modified, staged, or untracked.

items.name: git add (file)
items.definition: Stage a specific file for the next commit.

items.name: git add (all)
items.definition: Stage all changed and new files in the working directory.

items.name: git commit
items.definition: Record staged changes with a descriptive message.

items.name: git commit (all)
items.definition: Stage all tracked file changes and commit in one step.

items.name: git restore
items.definition: Discard unstaged changes in the working directory for a file.

items.name: git restore --staged
items.definition: Unstage a file while keeping its changes in the working directory.

items.name: git reset (file)
items.definition: Unstage a file without modifying its contents.

items.name: git reset --hard
items.definition: Revert all uncommitted changes and return to the last commit state.

items.name: git diff
items.definition: Show unstaged differences between the working directory and the index.

items.name: git diff --staged
items.definition: Show changes staged for the next commit but not yet committed.

items.name: git rebase
items.definition: Reapply commits from the current branch on top of another branch.

items.name: config user.name
items.definition: Set the name that will appear on all commits globally.

items.name: config user.email
items.definition: Set the email address that will appear on all commits globally.

items.name: config color.ui
items.definition: Enable automatic colored output in the terminal.

items.name: config --edit
items.definition: Open the global Git configuration file in the default text editor.

items.name: git branch
items.definition: List all local branches in the repository.

items.name: git branch -av
items.definition: List all local and remote branches with their latest commits.

items.name: git checkout
items.definition: Switch to an existing branch and update the working directory.

items.name: git checkout -b
items.definition: Create a new branch and immediately switch to it.

items.name: git branch -d
items.definition: Delete a local branch (only if it has been fully merged).

items.name: git merge
items.definition: Merge the specified branch into the currently active branch.

items.name: git tag
items.definition: Create a lightweight tag pointing to the current commit.

items.name: git log
items.definition: Display the full commit history for the active branch.

items.name: git log (range)
items.definition: Show commits in branchA that are not yet in branchB.

items.name: git log --follow
items.definition: Track the change history of a file, including across renames.

items.name: git diff (branches)
items.definition: Show the diff between what is in branchA but not in branchB.

items.name: git show
items.definition: Display the contents and metadata of a specific commit by its SHA.

items.name: git fetch
items.definition: Download all branches from a remote without merging.

items.name: git merge (remote)
items.definition: Merge a remote-tracking branch into the current local branch.

items.name: git merge --no-ff
items.definition: Merge without fast-forwarding, always creating a merge commit.

items.name: git merge --ff-only
items.definition: Merge only if the branch can be fast-forwarded; abort otherwise.

items.name: git push
items.definition: Upload local branch commits to the remote repository.

items.name: git pull
items.definition: Fetch from the tracked remote and merge into the current branch.

items.name: git cherry-pick
items.definition: Apply the changes from a specific commit onto the current branch.

items.name: git remote add
items.definition: Register a new remote repository under a short alias.

items.name: git remote
items.definition: List the names of all configured remote connections.

items.name: git remote -v
items.definition: List all remotes along with their fetch and push URLs.

items.name: git remote rm
items.definition: Remove a remote connection from the repository.

items.name: git remote set-url
items.definition: Update the URL of an existing remote (e.g. after a repo migration).

items.name: git stash
items.definition: Save modified and staged changes onto a temporary stack.

items.name: git stash list
items.definition: Show all entries currently saved in the stash stack.

items.name: git stash pop
items.definition: Apply the most recent stash entry and remove it from the stack.

items.name: git stash drop
items.definition: Discard the most recent stash entry without applying it.

items.name: git rm
items.definition: Delete a file from the working directory and stage the removal.

items.name: git mv
items.definition: Move or rename a file and stage the change.

items.name: git log --stat -M
items.definition: Show commit logs with a summary of file movements and renames.

items.name: branch -m
items.definition: Rename the currently checked-out local branch.

items.name: push renamed
items.definition: Push the renamed branch to origin and set upstream tracking.

items.name: delete old remote
items.definition: Remove the old branch name from the remote repository.

items.name: log -S (search)
items.definition: Search commit history for changes that add or remove a specific string.

items.name: log -p (file)
items.definition: Show the full diff of every commit that touched a specific file.

items.name: log --graph
items.definition: Print a visual ASCII graph of the full branch and merge history.

items.name: branch -vv
items.definition: List branches with their upstream tracking info and last commit.

items.name: checkout -
items.definition: Switch back to the previously checked-out branch.

items.name: branch -r
items.definition: List only remote-tracking branches.

items.name: checkout file
items.definition: Restore a single file from another branch without switching branches.

items.name: commit --amend
items.definition: Replace the most recent commit with an updated message or content.

items.name: alias co
items.definition: Create a shorthand `git co` for the checkout command.

items.name: alias br
items.definition: Create a shorthand `git br` for the branch command.

items.name: alias ci
items.definition: Create a shorthand `git ci` for the commit command.

items.name: alias st
items.definition: Create a shorthand `git st` for the status command.
